newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto's party says her ouster unconstitutional.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's party says her ouster unconstitutional.

text.p: The Pakistan People's Party (PPP) said on Tuesday that the president's dismissal of its leader Benazir Bhutto as prime minister was unconstitutional.
A PPP statement said party leaders would meet on Wednesday to discuss what it called "the unconstitutional dismissal of the elected government in the darkness of night".

The secretary general of the PPP's executive committee, Rafique Ahmed, urged all its members to join Wednesday's emergency meeting and said PPP provincial branch leaders should also hold meetings to chart the party's future line of action.

The statement was the party's first official reaction to an overnight proclamation by President Farooq Leghari in which he dissolved parliament and sacked Bhutto, accusing her three-year-old government of corruption and nepotism.
Leghari, once a PPP member, named veteran politician Meraj Khalid to head a caretaker administration to supervise general elections, set by the president for February 3, 1997.

A PPP official said Bhutto would preside over Wednesday's meeting if she was at liberty. Police have turned away former ministers who tried to visit Bhutto at her official residence near the presidential palace in Islamabad and her telephone lines have not worked since she was sacked.
